passages.title: Hope is the thing with feathers
passages.full_text:
"Hope" is the thing with feathers -
That perches in the soul -
And sings the tune without the words -
And never stops - at all -

And sweetest - in the Gale - is heard -
And sore must be the storm -
That could abash the little Bird
That kept so many warm -

I've heard it in the chillest land -
And on the strangest Sea -
Yet - never - in Extremity,
It asked a crumb - of Me.
passages.translation:
“希望”是长着羽毛的事物——
栖居在灵魂深处——
唱着无词的曲调——
永不停歇——丝毫不止——

在狂风中听来最甜蜜——
那风暴必定猛烈——
才能惊扰这只小鸟——
它曾温暖了那么多人——

我曾在最寒冷的大地上听见它——
在最陌生的海洋上——
然而——在绝境中——它从未——
向我索取过一丝面包屑。

key_sentence_patterns.explanation: 使用破折号和比喻结构，将抽象概念具体化。例如："Hope is the thing with feathers - That perches in the soul"
倒装和破折号强调地点和时间。例如："And sweetest - in the Gale - is heard"
用破折号分隔的并列状语，表示转折和强调。例如："Yet - never - in Extremity, / It asked a crumb - of Me"

key_grammar.example: 将“希望”比喻为“长着羽毛的事物”（a bird），通过意象传达希望的特征。
诗中使用大量破折号表示停顿、强调或分隔并列成分，如"And never stops - at all -"
每节第二行和第四行押韵：soul/all, storm/warm, Sea/Me，形成 ABCB 韵式。

passages.common_mistakes: 学习者可能忽略破折号在诗歌中表达的语气停顿，将其视为普通标点；或混淆押韵模式（实际为 ABCB 而非 AABB）。

passages.title: Good Morning
passages.full_text: Good morning sun, good morning sky. Open eyes, stretch up high. Brush teeth, comb hair. Eat breakfast, say a prayer. Ready for day. Happy morning!
passages.translation: 早上好，太阳，早上好，天空。睁开眼睛，向上伸展。刷牙，梳头。吃早餐，做个祈祷。准备好迎接新的一天。快乐的早晨！

key_sentence_patterns.explanation: Use this pattern to greet someone or something in the morning. Example: Good morning, sun.
Imperative verb phrase telling someone to open a body part. Example: Open eyes.
Expression meaning prepared for something. Example: Ready for day.

key_grammar.example: Brush teeth, comb hair, eat breakfast.

key_grammar.point: Simple present tense (for actions in routine)
key_grammar.example: I brush my teeth every morning. (implied)
Stretch high (adverb after verb)

passages.common_mistakes: Forgetting possessive determiners like 'my' before body parts (e.g., 'brush teeth' instead of 'brush my teeth') – though the rhyme omits them for rhythm, in standard English, 'my' is often used. Also, using 'good morning' only at the start, not as a general greeting.

Waiter: Good evening. Welcome to Bella Italia. How many people?

Could you bring the menu? (implied) / 'please' softens the request.

passages.title: Letter to the Editor
passages.full_text:
Dear Editor,

I have read your recent article about improving our community and I want to add my voice. I am writing to express my concern about the lack of public benches in our neighborhood. Many elderly residents have no place to sit and rest when they go for a walk. This is a serious problem because it makes it difficult for them to enjoy the outdoors and stay active. I am not alone in this opinion; many of my neighbors agree.

Last week, I saw an old woman sitting on the ground because she was tired. Her legs hurt and she needed a break. This situation is not acceptable in a modern city. Other cities have many benches in parks and along streets. Why can't our city do the same? Benches are simple and cheap but they make a big difference.

I think the local government should install more benches in public areas. They are not expensive and they help people of all ages. Children can sit while playing, adults can rest after shopping, and elderly people can take breaks during their walks. Benches also encourage social interaction. People can meet and talk while sitting.

Furthermore, benches improve the appearance of the neighborhood. A park with benches looks more welcoming. I hope you will publish this letter and bring attention to this issue. Thank you for your time.

Sincerely,
A Concerned Resident
passages.translation:
尊敬的编辑：

我阅读了您最近关于改善社区的文章，也想表达我的看法。我写这封信是想表达我对我们街区缺乏公共长椅的担忧。许多老年居民散步时没有地方可以坐下休息。这是一个严重的问题，因为它让他们难以享受户外活动和保持活力。我并不是唯一有这种想法的人，我的许多邻居也同意。

上周，我看到一位老妇人因为累了坐在地上。她的腿疼，需要休息一下。这种情况在一个现代化城市中是不可接受的。其他城市在公园和街道旁都有很多长椅。为什么我们的城市不能这样做呢？长椅简单又便宜，但作用很大。

我认为当地政府应该在公共区域安装更多长椅。它们不贵，而且能帮助各个年龄段的人。孩子们可以边玩边坐，成年人购物后可以休息，老年人散步时可以歇脚。长椅还能促进社交互动，人们可以坐着见面聊天。

此外，长椅能改善社区面貌。有长椅的公园看起来更宜人。我希望您能刊登这封信，引起对这一问题的关注。感谢您的时间。

此致
一位关心的居民

key_sentence_patterns.pattern: I am writing to express my concern about...
key_sentence_patterns.explanation: Use this pattern to begin a letter and state the main issue you want to discuss.
Use this to give an opinion or make a suggestion.
Use this rhetorical question to emphasize a point or express frustration.

key_grammar.point: Present perfect for recent experiences or actions
key_grammar.example: I have read your recent article. / I have seen an old woman sitting on the ground.
I think the local government should install more benches.

key_grammar.point: Simple past for specific past events
key_grammar.example: Last week, I saw an old woman sitting on the ground.

common_mistakes: Incorrect: 'I am concern about' → Correct: 'I am concerned about'
Incorrect: 'benefits' as verb singular → Correct: 'benefit' (e.g., 'They benefit people')

passages.title: Marie Curie and Her Discoveries
passages.full_text: Marie Curie was a famous scientist. She was born in Poland in 1867. She moved to France to study at the University of Paris. At the university, she met a scientist named Pierre Curie, and they got married. Together, they studied radioactivity. Marie Curie discovered two new elements: polonium and radium. She built special machines to measure radiation. Her work was very important for medicine. Later, she won two Nobel Prizes. One was for Physics in 1903, and the other was for Chemistry in 1911. She was the first woman to win a Nobel Prize. Marie Curie died in 1934. Her discoveries helped many scientists after her. Today, Marie Curie is still remembered as a pioneer in science. She showed that women can be great scientists too.
passages.translation: 玛丽·居里是一位著名的科学家。她于1867年出生在波兰。她移居法国，在巴黎大学学习。在大学里，她遇到了一位名叫皮埃尔·居里的科学家，他们结婚了。他们一起研究放射性。玛丽·居里发现了两种新元素：钋和镭。她制造了特殊的仪器来测量辐射。她的工作对医学非常重要。后来，她获得了两次诺贝尔奖。一次是1903年的物理学奖，另一次是1911年的化学奖。她是第一位获得诺贝尔奖的女性。玛丽·居里于1934年去世。她的发现帮助了许多后来的科学家。如今，玛丽·居里仍然作为科学先驱被人们铭记。她证明了女性也可以成为伟大的科学家。

key_sentence_patterns.explanation: Used to introduce someone's birth year and place.
Used to state a scientific discovery.
Used to describe how someone is known historically.

key_grammar.point: Past simple tense for completed actions
key_grammar.example: Marie Curie discovered two new elements.
She is still remembered as a pioneer.
Today, Marie Curie is still remembered.

passages.common_mistakes: Using present simple instead of past simple for completed historical events (e.g., 'She discovers radium' instead of 'She discovered radium').

passages.title: The Story of Steve Jobs
passages.source: Original content based on historical facts
passages.full_text:
Steve Jobs was born in 1955 in California. He was adopted as a baby and grew up in Silicon Valley. As a teenager, he became interested in electronics and met Steve Wozniak, a computer expert. In 1976, Jobs and Wozniak founded Apple Computer in Jobs's garage. They created the Apple I, a simple computer for hobbyists. The Apple II, released later, became very popular and made Apple a successful company.

In 1985, after a conflict with the board of directors, Jobs left Apple. He started a new company called NeXT, which made powerful computers for education and business. NeXT was not a big commercial success, but its technology was very advanced. During this time, Jobs also bought a small animation studio from George Lucas. He renamed it Pixar. Pixar created the first fully computer-animated film, Toy Story, in 1995. The film was a huge success, and Pixar became a major player in Hollywood.

In 1997, Apple bought NeXT, and Jobs returned to the company as CEO. He brought new ideas and a focus on design. Under his leadership, Apple launched the iMac, iPod, iPhone, and iPad. These products changed the way people use technology. Jobs was known for his perfectionism and his vision. He believed in making products that were simple, beautiful, and easy to use.

Steve Jobs died in 2011 after a long battle with cancer. His legacy lives on in the products we use every day. He showed that one person's imagination can change the world.
passages.translation:
史蒂夫·乔布斯于1955年出生于加利福尼亚州。他出生后被收养，在硅谷长大。十几岁时，他对电子学产生了兴趣，并结识了电脑专家史蒂夫·沃兹尼亚克。1976年，乔布斯和沃兹尼亚克在乔布斯的车库里创立了苹果电脑公司。他们制造了Apple I，这是一款面向爱好者的简单电脑。后来发布的Apple II非常受欢迎，使苹果成为一家成功的公司。

1985年，在与董事会发生冲突后，乔布斯离开了苹果。他创办了一家名为NeXT的新公司，生产用于教育和商业的强力电脑。NeXT在商业上并非大获成功，但其技术非常先进。在此期间，乔布斯还从乔治·卢卡斯手中收购了一家小型动画工作室。他将其更名为皮克斯。皮克斯制作了第一部完全由电脑生成的动画电影《玩具总动员》，于1995年上映。该片大获成功，皮克斯成为好莱坞的重要力量。

1997年，苹果收购了NeXT，乔布斯回到公司担任CEO。他带来了新的理念，并对设计高度重视。在他的领导下，苹果推出了iMac、iPod、iPhone和iPad。这些产品改变了人们使用科技的方式。乔布斯以其完美主义和远见卓识而闻名。他相信制造简单、美观且易于使用的产品。

史蒂夫·乔布斯在与癌症长期斗争后于2011年去世。他的遗产存在于我们每天使用的产品中。他展示了一个人的想象力可以改变世界。

key_sentence_patterns.explanation: Used to talk about someone's birth, a common structure in biographies.
Used to describe how someone started to like or care about something.
Used to describe the creation or start of a company, product, or project.

key_sentence_patterns.pattern: Under + possessive + leadership / guidance, subject + verb...
key_sentence_patterns.explanation: Used to describe achievements or changes that happened while someone was in charge.

key_grammar.example: He was born in 1955. / He became interested in electronics and met Steve Wozniak.
He was adopted as a baby. / The film was a huge success.
Jobs, who was known for his perfectionism, ... / NeXT, which made powerful computers, ...

passages.common_mistakes: 1. Confusing 'its' (possessive) with 'it's' (it is). E.g., 'its technology' not 'it's technology'. 2. Using 'used to' incorrectly for past habits that no longer happen. E.g., 'He used to work at Apple' is correct; 'He used to be CEO' implies he no longer is. 3. Forgetting to use past tense for actions completed in the past, e.g., 'He founded Apple' not 'He founds Apple'.

passages.title: On the Pleasure of Hating
passages.source: Adapted from William Hazlitt's essay 'On the Pleasure of Hating' (1826)
passages.full_text:
Why do we enjoy hating? It is a strange question, but one that many people have thought about. William Hazlitt, an English writer from the 19th century, believed that hating others gives us a secret pleasure. He thought that this feeling is natural to human beings.

Hazlitt said that we often hate people who are different from us. For example, we might dislike someone because of their political views, their success, or even their happiness. When we see others fail, we sometimes feel a little satisfaction. This is not a nice thought, but Hazlitt argued that it is true.

He explained that hating makes us feel more powerful. When we hate someone, we put ourselves above them. We think, 'I am better than that person.' This gives us a sense of control. Also, hating can bring people together. Groups often unite against a common enemy. This shared hatred creates a bond.

But Hazlitt warned that this pleasure is dangerous. If we enjoy hating too much, we become bitter and lonely. We start to see faults in everyone and everything. Our relationships suffer, and we lose the ability to enjoy love and friendship.

In modern times, we can see this idea everywhere. Social media often encourages hatred. People attack others for their opinions or appearances. They feel pleasure when they 'win' an argument or make someone look bad. But this kind of pleasure is empty. It does not make us happier in the long run.

Hazlitt's essay reminds us to be careful. It is natural to feel anger or dislike sometimes, but we should not let these feelings control us. Instead, we should try to understand others and find pleasure in kindness and cooperation. The real pleasure in life comes not from hating, but from loving and connecting with others.
passages.translation:
为什么我们享受憎恨？这是一个奇怪的问题，但很多人都思考过。威廉·赫兹里特，一位19世纪的英国作家，相信憎恨他人会带给我们一种隐秘的愉悦。他认为这种感受是人类的天性。
赫兹里特说，我们经常憎恨那些与我们不同的人。例如，我们可能因为某人的政治观点、成功甚至幸福而不喜欢他们。当我们看到别人失败时，有时会感到一丝满足。这不是一个美好的想法，但赫兹里特认为这是事实。
他解释说，憎恨让我们感觉自己更强大。当我们憎恨某人时，我们把自己置于他们之上。我们想：“我比那个人更好。”这给了我们一种控制感。此外，憎恨可以让人们团结在一起。群体常常联合起来对抗共同的敌人。这种共同的憎恨产生了一种纽带。
但赫兹里特警告说，这种愉悦是危险的。如果我们太享受憎恨，就会变得苦涩和孤独。我们开始看到每个人和每件事的缺点。我们的人际关系受损，失去了享受爱与友谊的能力。
在现代，我们到处都能看到这种观点。社交媒体常常鼓励憎恨。人们因他人的观点或外表而攻击他们。当他们“赢得”一场争论或让他人难堪时，他们会感到愉悦。但这种愉悦是空洞的。从长远来看，它并不会让我们更快乐。
赫兹里特的文章提醒我们要小心。有时感到愤怒或不喜欢是自然的，但我们不应该让这些情绪控制我们。相反，我们应该尝试理解他人，并在善意与合作中找到愉悦。生活中真正的愉悦不是来自憎恨，而是来自爱和与他人连接。

key_sentence_patterns.explanation: Used to introduce a question about a common human experience. The pattern 'enjoy + gerund' shows a habitual pleasure.

key_sentence_patterns.pattern: It is [adjective] to [verb] ... but one that ...
key_sentence_patterns.explanation: A structure to present a statement that is paradoxical or surprising. 'One that' refers back to the noun.
A conditional-like pattern showing cause and effect in general situations. Useful for describing typical behavior.
Used to report someone's opinion in a persuasive way. Common in argumentative texts.

key_grammar.example: We enjoy hating.
Hating makes us feel more powerful.
This shared hatred can create a bond.
We should not let these feelings control us.

common_mistakes: Using 'hate' as a noun incorrectly: 'hate' is a verb or noun; 'hating' is the gerund form. Learners often say 'I have hate' instead of 'I feel hatred' or 'I hate'. In this text, 'hating' is used as a gerund.
Confusing 'enjoy + to verb' with 'enjoy + verb-ing': The correct pattern is 'enjoy hating', not 'enjoy to hate'.
Misuse of 'but' as a conjunction: In the pattern 'It is strange, but one that...', 'but' connects two contrasting ideas. Learners may omit the comma or use 'however' incorrectly.
Overuse of 'very' before adjectives like 'powerful' – in B2, it is better to use more precise adverbs like 'extremely' or 'quite'.
